disks.name: CP/M 2.2 (MITS, 63K)
disks.license: Free to redistribute (DRDOS Inc. CP/M license, 2001, reconfirmed 2022).
disks.description: Bootable MITS/Altair CP/M 2.2 for a 63K system with the 88-2SIO console. Mike Douglas's DISK01 from altairclone.com.
disks.help:
A stock CP/M 2.2 system disk. Handy programs on it:

  ED name.txt   line editor, very terse:
                  I       start inserting text; end with Ctrl-Z
                  E       save and exit       Q  quit, no save
  ASM name      assemble name.ASM  ->  name.HEX
  LOAD name     name.HEX  ->  name.COM
  DDT name.COM  8080 debugger.  G runs,  Ctrl-C leaves it
  DUMP name     hex-dump a file
  MBASIC        Microsoft BASIC.  Leave it with:  SYSTEM
  STAT          disk space and file sizes
  PIP B:=A:*.*  copy every file from A: to B:

disks.name: CP/M Games
disks.needs: 64K RAM, drive A:, a CRT terminal
disks.license: Old hobbyist games, freely passed around since the early 1980s.
disks.description: CP/M game disk (dhansel DISK05). Boots CP/M on its own.
disks.help:
CATCHUM       a Pac-Man clone           press Q to quit
  LADDER        a climbing game            Ctrl-C to quit
  OTHELLO       reversi against the computer
  STARTRK.BAS   run with:  MBASIC STARTRK   (leave BASIC: SYSTEM)
  LUNAR.BAS     run with:  MBASIC LUNAR

Switch the Terminal dropdown to "DEC VT100" first -- these move
the cursor around and expect a real CRT.

disks.name: Altair DOS 1.0
disks.license: Orphaned. MITS closed in 1979 and nobody has claimed it since.
disks.description: MITS Altair DOS 1.0 (dhansel DISK02) - the pre-CP/M MITS disk operating system.
disks.help:
MITS Altair DOS 1.0. The prompt is  .  (a period).
  .DIR          list files
  .MNT 0        mount the disk in drive 0
  .name         run a program
This is here for historical interest; CP/M superseded it fast.

disks.name: Altair Disk Extended BASIC 300-5-F
disks.needs: 64K RAM, drive A:, sense switches down
disks.license: Same standing as the Altair BASIC tapes on this page. MITS is long gone and nobody objects.
disks.description: MITS Disk Extended BASIC, version 300-5-F from May 1979. It boots straight into BASIC, no CP/M. Mike Douglas's DISK03.
disks.help:
Answer the cold-start questions:

  MEMORY SIZE?            Return uses all of it
  LINEPRINTER?            C, O, P or Q.  Any of them is fine
  HIGHEST DISK NUMBER?    1 if you want drive B: too
  HOW MANY FILES?         3
  HOW MANY RANDOM FILES?  2

Then at OK:

  MOUNT 0       mount drive A:  (MOUNT 0,1 for both)
  FILES         list files.  FILES 1 lists drive B:
  LOAD "NAME"   load a program.  LOAD "NAME",1 from B:
  RUN           run it
  SAVE "NAME"   save it
  UNLOAD        before you eject a disk

Put the BASIC Programs disk in B: for something to run.

disks.name: Disk BASIC Programs
disks.needs: Disk BASIC in A:, this disk in B:
disks.license: Type-in BASIC programs from the 1970s, freely passed around ever since.
disks.description: About 75 BASIC games and utilities for Disk BASIC: STARTREK, WUMPUS, LUNAR, HANGMAN, CHESS and more. Not bootable. Mike Douglas's DISK04.
disks.help:
Not a boot disk. Boot Disk BASIC in drive A:, put this one in
B:, answer 1 to HIGHEST DISK NUMBER?, then:

  MOUNT 0,1
  FILES 1                 list what's here
  RUN "STARTREK",1         load and run a program from B:

Some want a CRT. Switch the Terminal dropdown to "DEC VT100"
for the ones marked VT-100.

disks.name: WordStar 3.00
disks.needs: 64K RAM, drive A:, DEC VT52 terminal
disks.license: Commercial software, no formal redistribution grant. Shared by vintage-computing archives for decades.
disks.description: The word processor that made CP/M worth owning. Boots CP/M with WordStar ready to go. Mike Douglas's DISK07.
disks.help:
Set the Terminal dropdown to "DEC VT52" first. This copy is
installed for a VT52.

  WS            start WordStar
  D             open a document file (type a name)
  Ctrl-K D      save and go back to the menu
  Ctrl-K Q      quit without saving
  X             back to CP/M from the menu

The cursor diamond: Ctrl-E up, Ctrl-X down, Ctrl-S left,
Ctrl-D right.

disks.name: SuperCalc2 1.00
disks.needs: 64K RAM, drive A:, DEC VT100 terminal
disks.license: Commercial software, no formal redistribution grant. Shared by vintage-computing archives for decades.
disks.description: Sorcim's spreadsheet, installed for a VT100. Boots CP/M. Mike Douglas's DISK06.
disks.help:
Set the Terminal dropdown to a DEC VT100 first.

  SC2           start SuperCalc
  Return        past the title screen
  /             the command menu
  ?             help
  /Q Y          quit back to CP/M

Type a number or a formula into a cell and press Return.
Start text with a quote mark (").

disks.name: Zork I, II and III
disks.license: The Zork I-III source has been MIT licensed since November 2025. The Infocom CP/M interpreter isn't covered by that.
disks.description: All three Zorks for CP/M. Zork I is Revision 88, serial 840726. Boots CP/M. Mike Douglas's DISK08.
disks.help:
ZORK1         The Great Underground Empire
  ZORK2         The Wizard of Frobozz
  ZORK3         The Dungeon Master

Type in plain English:  OPEN MAILBOX,  GO NORTH,  TAKE LAMP.
  SAVE / RESTORE    save your game to the disk
  QUIT              back to CP/M

Any terminal works, even the Teletype.

disks.name: CP/M 3.0 (boot disk)
disks.license: Free to redistribute (DRDOS Inc. CP/M license, 2001, reconfirmed 2022).
disks.description: CP/M Plus, non-banked, with an Altair 8" floppy BIOS. Comes with MBASIC, SID, RMAC and LINK. Mike Douglas's DISK13.
disks.help:
CP/M 3 is CP/M 2.2 with friendlier tools.

  DIR           with options, e.g.  DIR [FULL]
  TYPE name     show a text file, a page at a time
  ERASE name    delete a file
  RENAME        rename a file
  SHOW          disk space
  DEVICE        list and set the character devices
  MBASIC        Microsoft BASIC.  SYSTEM leaves it

README.TXT on this disk has Mike Douglas's notes.
The utilities disk goes in B: for more.

disks.name: CP/M 3.0 (utilities)
disks.license: Free to redistribute (DRDOS Inc. CP/M license, 2001, reconfirmed 2022).
disks.description: The second CP/M 3.0 disk: HELP, MAC, LIB, GENCOM, SET, DATE and the rest. Boots on its own too. Mike Douglas's DISK14.
disks.help:
HELP          CP/M 3's own help system.  HELP DIR, HELP SET...
  MAC name      macro assembler
  LIB           library manager
  SET           file attributes and passwords
  DATE          set or show the date
  INITDIR       add date stamps to a disk
